title: What causes StackOverflowError (unbounded recursion, cyclic toString/equals), how does it differ from OutOfMemoryError, and how to prevent it?
keyPoints: StackOverflowError occurs when the per-thread call stack (512KB to 1MB) is exhausted by too many nested method calls
Common causes: unbounded recursion (missing base case), mutual recursion (A calls B calls A), cyclic toString/equals in JPA entities
OutOfMemoryError occurs when the shared JVM heap is full, caused by memory leaks or large data loads
SOE is per-thread (one thread dies), OOM is JVM-wide (everything affected)
Fix SOE: add base case, convert recursion to iteration, exclude parent references in JPA toString
Fix OOM: profile with heap dumps, fix memory leaks, increase -Xmx, use streaming/pagination

s1_definition.oneliner: StackOverflowError is caused by exhausting the per-thread call stack through unbounded recursion, while OutOfMemoryError is caused by exhausting the shared JVM heap through memory leaks or large data.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **StackOverflowError** = the per-thread call stack (default 512KB to 1MB) is exhausted. Each method call pushes a frame. Causes: unbounded recursion, mutual recursion, cyclic toString/equals.
- **OutOfMemoryError** = the shared JVM heap (default 256MB to 4GB) is full. Causes: memory leaks, loading all records into memory, classloader leaks.
- Key difference: SOE is **per-thread** (stack depth). OOM is **JVM-wide** (heap space). SOE is usually a code bug. OOM is usually a memory leak or undersized heap.
s1_definition.analogy: StackOverflowError: a teller at National Bank of India keeps opening sub-requests inside sub-requests (recursion) until their desk collapses under the paperwork. Each teller has a small desk (512KB stack). OutOfMemoryError: the entire bank vault (shared heap) is full with too many safe deposit boxes. SOE affects one desk. OOM affects the whole bank.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  StackOverflowError:          OutOfMemoryError:
  ┌──────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────┐
  │ Thread Stack      │        │ JVM Heap              │
  │ (per thread)      │        │ (shared)              │
  │ ~512KB-1MB        │        │ ~256MB-4GB            │
  │                   │        │                       │
  │ frame(n)          │        │ Object Object Object  │
  │ frame(n-1)        │        │ Object Object Object  │
  │ frame(n-2)        │        │ Object ... full ...   │
  │ ... overflow ...  │        │ No room for new obj   │
  └──────────────────┘        └──────────────────────┘
  Fix: base case,             Fix: fix leak,
  iteration, -Xss             -Xmx, profiler
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
StackOverflowError occurs when the per-thread call stack is exhausted by too many nested method calls. The most common causes are unbounded recursion (missing base case), mutual recursion (A calls B calls A), and cyclic toString/equals in JPA entities with bidirectional relationships. OutOfMemoryError occurs when the shared JVM heap is full from memory leaks or loading too much data into memory.

The key difference: SOE is per-thread (one thread dies, others continue) while OOM is JVM-wide (everything is affected). SOE is usually a code bug fixed by adding a base case or converting to iteration. OOM is usually a memory leak fixed by profiling with heap dumps.

At National Bank of India, the trade processing service had a cyclic toString between Account and Trade entities. Logging a trade triggered Account.toString() which called Trade.toString() which called Account.toString() in an infinite loop. Fix: exclude the parent reference with @ToString.Exclude in Lombok.

Remember one sentence: StackOverflowError is per-thread recursion exhaustion while OutOfMemoryError is JVM-wide heap exhaustion.
